Uttar Pradesh government's AYUSH Minister Dr. Dayashankar Mishra Dayalu has started using an electric vehicle (EV) single car. Meanwhile, Varanasi MLA Saurabh Srivastava went out on a bicycle for area visits. During this, he appealed to the public to use bicycles and walk. Actually, late Tuesday night, CM Yogi Adityanath had appealed to ministers and MLAs to use public transport one day a week. BJP workers also took out a rally on e-scooters to make Varanasi residents aware and reduce petrol-diesel consumption. In the rally, workers holding flags raised slogans in support of Narendra Modi. See 4 pictures... Minister requests people to use EVs In Varanasi, AYUSH Minister Dr. Dayashankar Mishra 'Dayalu' appealed to the residents of Kashi and the state to adopt electric vehicles and fuel-saving measures as much as possible. In compliance with the directives of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dr. Dayashankar Mishra Dayalu has started using an electric vehicle (EV) single car. He said that public participation is extremely necessary for building a clean and green Uttar Pradesh. Dr. Dayashankar Mishra 'Dayalu' said - Environmental protection, pollution control and fuel conservation are the biggest needs of today's time. Inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Green India" vision and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's environment-friendly policies, he has started using EV vehicles. In the coming time, he will also adopt many other environment-friendly changes in his daily life, so that a positive message about fuel and clean environment reaches society. Only when public representatives themselves take initiative in this direction will widespread awareness be created in society and this campaign can take the form of a mass movement. Varanasi MLA rode a bicycle Varanasi MLA Saurabh Srivastava toured the area on a bicycle. He said - In view of the war, PM Modi appealed to save resources and diesel-petrol. He himself reduced the vehicles in his convoy. Taking inspiration from PM Modi, I have also started cycling instead of using a car. Right now I am going for an area tour. My request to everyone is that if you have to go a short distance within the city, then walk or go by bicycle. This is good for both your health and the country. Jai Hind Jai Bharat. Awareness rally taken out on e-scooters in Varanasi In Varanasi, BJP has started an awareness campaign regarding petrol and diesel by riding electric scooters. BJP workers reached out to the masses regarding PM Modi's appeal. Workers appealed for consumption of petrol and diesel as per requirement. Garlanding and with folded hands, appealing to people to use petrol and diesel minimally. Support us in the nation's interest. Stickers of PM's appeal were also pasted at petrol pumps and public places. In the rally, workers raised slogans of Modi ji's path for the nation's sake. Yesterday Yogi took major decisions amid the energy crisis PM Modi said for 2 consecutive days - Reduce the use of petrol-diesel Prime Minister Narendra Modi said from a public platform on May 10 and 11 that in today's times, the use of petrol-diesel and gas will have to be reduced. Due to the impact of the war going on in the neighborhood, petrol-diesel prices have increased manifold across the world. India is more affected by this global crisis. We don't have large oil wells. Today we need measures like work from home. In cities where there is metro, people should use the metro. He said that earlier when there was war, people used to donate gold. Today there is no need for donation, but we have to take this pledge today that for the next 1 year, whatever program there is, don't buy gold. This will also save foreign exchange. stories.title: CBI, ED summoned in Rahul Gandhi assets case:High Court seeks response within 8 weeks
stories.summary: The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court has sought responses from multiple central agencies in connection with allegations of disproportionate assets against Rahul Gandhi. The court directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Enforcement Directorate (ED), and the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), along with other concerned departments, to file their replies within eight weeks. The next hearing in the matter has been scheduled for July 20. The order was passed by a division bench comprising Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan and Justice Zafeer Ahmad while hearing a petition filed by S. Vignesh Shishir. The petitioner also requested that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), the Revenue Department under the Finance Ministry, and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs be made parties to the case. The court accepted the request. Petitioner claims complaints already submitted to CBI, ED During the hearing, counsel representing the CBI informed the court that the petitioner’s complaint had already been received and that a response regarding the inquiry would be submitted by the next hearing date. Similarly, the ED told the court that the allegations were being examined after receipt of the complaint and that a progress report would be filed during the next hearing. The court observed that if the complaint had already been received, the concerned agencies should verify the allegations in accordance with the law and take necessary action. The SFIO also sought additional time to submit its response, which was granted by the court. All parties have been directed to file their affidavits within the stipulated timeframe. Court orders records to be kept in sealed cover Considering the sensitivity of the matter, the High Court also ordered that the complete case records and related documents be preserved in a sealed cover. BJP worker from Karnataka filed the petition The petition was filed by Karnataka-based BJP worker S. Vignesh Shishir. The petitioner has alleged that Rahul Gandhi and members of his family possess assets disproportionate to their declared income. The plea has sought an impartial investigation by central agencies into the allegations. During the upcoming hearing, the court will first examine the maintainability of the petition — determining whether the plea is legally fit for detailed consideration. Further legal proceedings will depend on the outcome of that assessment.

stories.title: Pregnant woman murdered after dispute over clothing:Husband kills wife, then ends life; WhatsApp chats reveal repeated arguments
stories.summary: A shocking case of domestic violence has emerged from Gorakhpur, where a man allegedly strangled his pregnant wife to death over disputes related to her clothing choices before dying by suicide. The incident came to light after postmortem findings contradicted initial assumptions of a double suicide. Police said the husband was upset over his wife wearing lower-T-shirts and what he considered “modern clothes.” WhatsApp chats recovered from the couple’s phones allegedly revealed repeated arguments over her lifestyle and dressing preferences. The incident took place in the Belghat police station area of Gorakhpur. Bodies found inside locked room According to police, the couple had married for love around six months ago. On Tuesday morning, family members became suspicious after the room remained locked for an unusually long time. When the door was eventually broken open, the husband’s body was found hanging from a ceiling fan, while the pregnant wife’s body was lying on the bed. Foam was reportedly coming out of her mouth. Initially, police suspected it to be a case of suicide. However, the case took a dramatic turn after the postmortem report confirmed that the woman had died due to strangulation. Investigators then examined the couple’s mobile phones, social media accounts and WhatsApp chats, which allegedly revealed the reason behind the murder. WhatsApp chats revealed repeated arguments Police said the chats showed ongoing tension between the couple over lifestyle differences and clothing. In one message, the wife, Nikhat, allegedly told her husband Shadab: “You never take me out anywhere. You never buy anything for me. I am not a girl who can remain confined inside a house.” In response, Shadab reportedly wrote: “Girls from our community do not wear such clothes. If you want to live with me, you will have to stop wearing lower-T-shirts at home.” Police say relationship had been under stress According to SP South Dinesh Puri, the case initially appeared to be suicide, but the postmortem report and digital evidence revealed a different sequence of events. “A husband and wife were found dead inside a house. Initially, it appeared to be a suicide case. But the postmortem report and WhatsApp chats exposed the truth. The husband first killed his wife and then died by suicide by hanging himself,” he said. Police investigations further revealed that the relationship had been under stress for several days. “Nikhat was raised in Mumbai and was unable to adjust to the village environment. Tensions between the couple had increased significantly,” the officer added. According to investigators, Nikhat also taunted Shadab for being unemployed and having an orthodox mindset, which further worsened the relationship.

stories.title: Prateek's father-in-law performs his last rites:Both daughters present; Akhilesh pays final tribute to younger brother
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s younger brother Prateek Yadav was cremated on Thursday afternoon in Lucknow. Prateek’s father-in-law Arvind Singh Bisht, the father of BJP leader Aparna Yadav, lit the funeral pyre. Akhilesh placed wood on his brother’s pyre and paid his final respects. Prateek’s two daughters were also present at the cremation ground and performed the ritual by placing wood on the pyre. However, priest Dhruv Kumar Tiwari, who conducted the last rites, had earlier told Dainik Bhaskar that it would have been more appropriate if Akhilesh Yadav or his son had lit the pyre. Thousands accompany funeral procession Earlier in the day, Prateek’s funeral procession was taken out in Lucknow. Thousands of supporters walked alongside the procession, raising slogans of 'Prateek Yadav amar rahein'. Aditya Yadav, son of Shivpal Singh Yadav, helped carry the bier on his shoulders. SP office is located a short distance from Prateek’s residence. The body was briefly placed on the ground there. According to Hindu tradition, the body is placed on the ground five times before reaching the cremation ground. Animal lover remembered through funeral tribute Prateek was known for his love for animals. A photograph showing him with his dogs and a monkey was placed on the funeral vehicle. Earlier in the morning, his body was kept at home for people to pay their last respects. Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak paid tribute to him. Shivpal Yadav and Akhilesh’s wife Dimple Yadav also offered floral tributes. During the night, Aparna remained seated beside the body along with the couple’s two daughters. Died at 38; post-mortem cites cardiac arrest Prateek died at around 6 am on Wednesday at the age of 38. The post-mortem report stated cardiac arrest as the cause of death. Doctors found six injuries on his body that had occurred before his death. Of these, three injuries were around seven days old, while three were sustained a day earlier. His viscera has been preserved for further examination. Prateek was the son of late Mulayam Singh Yadav’s second wife Sadhana Gupta. His wife Aparna is a BJP leader and currently serves as vice-chairperson of the State Women’s Commission. According to doctors, Prateek was suffering from pulmonary embolism, a serious lung condition in which a blood clot blocks circulation in the lungs. Suffered two heart attacks within 13 days Doctors said Prateek had suffered two heart attacks within 13 days. On April 30, he had collapsed while walking at Lucknow airport. Doctors at Medanta Hospital had then confirmed that he had suffered a heart attack. See photos related to Prateek's funeral- Studied in Britain, stayed away from politics

stories.title: Storms, rain claim 104 lives across UP in 24 hours:Man blown away 50 feet with tin shed; power outage in 2,000 villages
stories.summary: Severe thunderstorms, heavy rain and lightning wreaked havoc across Uttar Pradesh over the past 24 hours, leaving at least 104 people dead and causing widespread destruction in several districts. The highest number of deaths was reported from Prayagraj is 21, Bhadohi reported 17. In Mirzapur, 15 people died due to thunderstorms and lightning strikes. Fatehpur reported nine deaths, while six people died in Badaun. Four deaths each were reported from Pratapgarh and Bareilly. Strong winds, hailstorms and rain lash 30 districts During the last 24 hours, rainfall was reported in nearly 30 districts, including Ghaziabad, Varanasi and Ayodhya. Mathura, Unnao and Prayagraj witnessed hailstorms along with heavy rain and strong winds. Several trees were uprooted and fell on roads and residential areas, disrupting normal life in many places. Man flung nearly 100 metres in Bareilly One of the most dramatic incidents was reported from Bareilly, where a young man was swept away along with a tin shed during strong winds. According to local reports, the youth was lifted nearly 45 feet into the air before being thrown into a field around 100 metres away. He suffered fractures in both arms and legs and is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital. Power outage in more than 2,000 villages The severe weather also disrupted electricity supply in more than 2,000 villages across districts such as Deoria, Barabanki and Sitapur. Restoration work is underway in affected regions. Banda recorded state’s highest temperature While storms affected several districts, Banda remained the hottest city in Uttar Pradesh, recording a maximum temperature of 45.4 degrees Celsius. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh from Lucknow said the western disturbance affecting the state is gradually weakening. “From today onward, the western disturbance will start weakening, leading to clearer weather conditions across the state. Temperatures will gradually rise, and both daytime and nighttime heat will increase. From May 16, heatwave conditions may intensify in Bundelkhand and southern districts,” he said. stories.title: Prateek suffered two heart attacks in 13 days:Mulayam Singh Yadav treated him equally with Akhilesh
stories.summary: The sudden death of Prateek Yadav (38), son of late former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav and stepbrother of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, has sparked emotional reactions across political and social circles in Uttar Pradesh. Family members, party supporters and close associates are now recalling lesser-known stories from his personal life, business journey and relationship with the Yadav family. Prateek, who suffered two heart attacks within 13 days, died on May 13 after reportedly collapsing at home in Lucknow. First heart attack came at Lucknow Airport According to family sources, Prateek suffered his first heart attack on April 30 at Lucknow’s Chaudhary Charan Singh Airport shortly after landing from a flight. As he was walking toward the VIP lounge, he reportedly experienced severe chest pain and dizziness before collapsing. His associates immediately rushed him to Medanta Hospital in Lucknow. Doctors diagnosed a mild cardiac arrest and said his life was saved because he reached the hospital on time. His wife Aparna Yadav also reached the hospital soon afterward. Doctors later informed him that he was suffering from hypertension and blood clotting-related complications. Despite medical advice to remain under observation and rest, Prateek reportedly insisted on being discharged. Doctors warned him about blood clotting After treatment for the first cardiac episode, doctors reportedly advised Prateek against exertion and asked him to continue monitoring his health. Medanta doctor Ruchika Sharma informed him about hypertension and blood clotting in the veins. However, Prateek left the hospital on May 3. On May 5, he underwent surgery for Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT), a condition involving blood clots in the legs, at another private hospital in Lucknow. He was discharged the following day and had been staying mostly confined to his room since then. Sources close to the family said he had reduced public interaction after the surgery. Aparna Yadav, who was on a visit to Assam at the time, remained in regular contact over phone calls. Second heart attack proved fatal On the morning of May 13, Prateek reportedly suffered another heart attack at home. He was rushed to Civil Hospital in Lucknow around 6:30 am, but doctors said he had already stopped breathing before arrival. After seeing his brother one final time, Akhilesh Yadav became emotional and reportedly said: “He was always careful about his health. I had told him to take care.” The second cardiac arrest proved fatal, ending a life that had often remained away from active politics despite belonging to one of Uttar Pradesh’s most influential political families. Mulayam Singh wanted Prateek in politics Prateek Yadav was not the biological son of late Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav. He was born to Sadhana Gupta from her first marriage with Chandra Prakash Gupta. This had once created apprehension within sections of the Yadav family, who feared political complications between Prateek and Akhilesh Yadav in the future. However, Mulayam Singh reportedly reassured the family that Akhilesh would remain the political heir and there would be no discrimination. At the same time, Mulayam also wanted Prateek to enter politics. He often discussed political matters with him and introduced him to senior party leaders. But Prateek consistently declined. According to people close to the family, he would often say: “I do not want to enter politics.” Grand wedding attended by bollywood celebrities Prateek married Aparna Bisht in 2011 in a lavish ceremony at Saifai. The wedding was attended by several prominent personalities including Amitabh Bachchan, Jaya Bachchan and Anil Kapoor. At the time, Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections were just months away. Guests at the wedding often jokingly asked Prateek when he would become an MLA. Family members recalled that he would smile, nod politely and respond: “I will think about it.” Business journey began after Akhilesh became CM In 2012, when Akhilesh Yadav became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Prateek stayed away from politics and entered the real estate business instead. Over time, he reportedly established around 16 companies and invested heavily in properties across Lucknow, Noida and Ghaziabad. His brother-in-law Aman alias Chandrashekhar Bisht was said to be closely associated with several of these ventures. Supporters wanted him to contest elections By 2013, speculation again intensified about Prateek entering politics. Reports emerged that he had begun interacting with party workers more actively. Posters demanding that he contest the 2014 Lok Sabha election from Azamgarh appeared outside party offices. Supporters raised slogans in his favour. When asked about contesting elections, Prateek clearly responded: “I have no intention of contesting elections.” Lamborghini purchase drew political attention In December 2016, months before the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Prateek purchased a Lamborghini Huracan reportedly worth ₹5.23 crore. At the time, he was considered the first person in Uttar Pradesh to own that luxury sports car model. He reportedly paid ₹73 lakh in cash while the remaining amount was financed through a bank loan. When Aparna Yadav filed her nomination from Lucknow Cantonment seat in 2017, Prateek drove her in the Lamborghini, attracting widespread public attention and criticism on social media because of his political connections. Responding to criticism, Prateek had said: “I am a businessman, not a politician. If you want to know about the car, come to my office and check the balance sheet.” Election affidavits later showed that he also had outstanding loans, including around ₹81.5 lakh borrowed from Akhilesh Yadav. Relationship with Akhilesh remained cordial Political circles often speculated about the relationship between Akhilesh and Prateek. People close to the family maintained that the relationship was normal and cordial, though neither publicly attempted to showcase excessive closeness. Interestingly, Prateek rarely posted photographs with Akhilesh on social media. His Instagram profile mostly featured pictures with Mulayam Singh Yadav instead. Animal welfare and love for travel Prateek also ran an animal welfare organisation called Jeev Ashray Foundation, which worked for stray animals. Even while hospitalised recently, he had reportedly posted a video regarding a Supreme Court-related issue involving stray dogs. Apart from business, he enjoyed international travel and luxury automobiles. He often travelled abroad with Aparna and their daughters. Last year, the family visited Sweden and Austria. He was also passionate about racing cars and attended motorsport-related events overseas. Divorce announcement shocked followers On January 19, 2026, Prateek surprised many by publicly announcing separation from Aparna Yadav. He had posted: “Aparna made my life hell.” However, within nine days, the couple reconciled. Sharing photographs together on Instagram, Prateek wrote: “All is Good. Champions are those who overcome personal and professional problems. We are a family of champions.” The couple was later seen together celebrating their daughter’s birthday in February, attended by several BJP leaders including Bhupendra Chaudhary and Neeraj Singh. Childhood and connection with Mulayam Singh Prateek was born on July 4, 1986. After his parents separated when he was around four years old, he stayed with his mother Sadhana Gupta in Lucknow. Sadhana had earlier worked at a hospital in Saifai, where she came into contact with Mulayam Singh’s family. Over time, she and Mulayam grew closer. During that period, Mulayam’s first wife Malti Devi and Akhilesh Yadav lived at the Chief Minister’s residence. Prateek frequently visited and sometimes stayed there along with other children in the family. Old photographs shared by him on social media showed Mulayam Singh interacting affectionately with children, including Prateek, long before he adopted the Yadav surname. Supporters often cite these moments to underline how Mulayam Singh treated Prateek like his own son despite there being no biological relation. A life between politics and privacy Though he belonged to one of India’s most influential political families, Prateek Yadav consciously stayed away from active politics. He built his identity through business, luxury lifestyle interests and social work, while remaining emotionally connected to the Yadav family. His sudden death has left supporters shocked, especially because he had survived a heart attack just days earlier. For many within the Samajwadi Party ecosystem, Prateek’s life remains a story of a man who had access to politics and power, yet repeatedly chose a quieter path outside electoral battles.

stories.title: Work from home policy announced in UP:Yogi cabinet mandates AC temperature limits, promotes public transport use
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday chaired the first Cabinet meeting after the recent expansion state ministry. Yogi announced several measures aimed at fuel conservation, energy efficiency, and promoting local economic activity. Addressing ministers at his official residence, CM said public representatives must set an example before citizens by adopting fuel-saving practices and reducing unnecessary expenditure. Two days work from home in large offices Yogi directed that offices with more than 50 employees should implement a “Work From Home” system for at least two days a week. He also instructed government offices to maintain air-conditioner temperatures between 24°C and 26°C and appealed for minimal use of lifts in secretariats and directorates. According to the CM, these steps are necessary in view of global fuel and energy challenges. Ministers asked to use public transport CM Yogi urged ministers to use public transport such as metro trains, buses, e-rickshaws, bicycles, and carpooling at least once every week. He said inter-district meetings, training sessions, and standing committee meetings of the Assembly and Legislative Council should increasingly be conducted through virtual mode to reduce travel and fuel consumption. ‘Unnecessary foreign travel should be avoided except in emergency situations’, he added. Fuel conservation a national responsibility CM said fuel conservation is not only an economic necessity but also a national responsibility under current global circumstances. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal for fuel saving, he said the Cabinet must lead by example so that society also adopts responsible practices. New EV policy and Solar awareness campaign planned Uttar Pradesh government will also prepare a new policy for electric vehicles (EVs). The Chief Minister directed officials to launch awareness campaigns promoting solar energy use in residential colonies, schools, and colleges. Push for domestic weddings and ‘vocal for local’ CM Yogi appealed for simplicity in social functions and asked citizens to prioritize domestic destinations for weddings and ceremonies to support the local economy. He also encouraged ministers to promote the “Vocal for Local” campaign by using gifts and products manufactured within Uttar Pradesh. Policy changes planned for PNG connections CM directed officials to prioritize PNG (Piped Natural Gas) connections over LPG cylinders and initiate necessary policy changes for faster implementation. He also stressed the need to shift commercial LPG users towards PNG connectivity. Awareness campaign against excessive oil consumption CM called for reducing dependence on imported products and promoting oilseed cultivation, natural farming, and balanced use of chemical fertilizers. He also asked departments to launch public awareness drives to reduce edible oil consumption, discourage unnecessary gold imports, and promote rainwater conservation as a mass movement. Meeting began with introduction of new ministers The Cabinet meeting began with the formal introduction of newly inducted ministers. CM Yogi advised the new ministers to learn from senior colleagues and develop effective administrative working styles. He also instructed Cabinet ministers to consult Ministers of State while taking policy-related decisions, emphasizing teamwork and accountability in governance.

stories.summary: The controversy surrounding Dhirendra Krishna Shastri of Bageshwar Dham's 'Divine Court' and his claims has heated up once again. The Maharashtra Andhashraddha Nirmoolan Samiti, completely rejecting the Baba's miracles, has now increased the challenge amount directly from Rs 30 lakh to Rs 80 lakh. The committee says that this fight is not against the Ramkatha, but against those claims being made in the guise of religion that do not stand up to the test of logic. Committee convener Shyam Manav had proposed the Nagpur Press Club venue for this challenge before Dhirendra Shastri, but the Baba has clearly stated that whoever wants to test him should come to the court. Now that Dhirendra Shastri has returned from Nagpur, Shyam Manav says that Shastri has failed to accept the challenge twice in a row and has fled once again. Bhaskar spoke with Anti-Superstition Eradication Committee convener Shyam Manav to understand why he is raising questions about the Baba's court. New Form of Challenge: Science's Rules Will Apply, Not Baba's The committee had made it clear that this time the contest will not be held in Baba's 'divine court', but at the 'Patrakar Bhavan' (Press Club) in Nagpur. The committee's reasoning behind this is that in Baba's own court, there could be many secret methods of gathering information, which are difficult to control. Challenge Conditions Still Remain 1. Neutral Ground: This test can only be conducted at Patrakar Bhavan in Nagpur. 2. Strict Monitoring: A panel committee will be formed, which will include Baba's consent as well. During the test, mobile phones of Baba and other people present there will be sealed. 3. 90% Accuracy Scale: 10 unknown persons will be suddenly brought before Baba. He will have to tell the names of those persons, their father's name, surname and mobile number. Additionally, he will have to identify 10 objects kept nearby using his 'divine vision'. 4. Double Test: If Baba succeeds the first time, then after 5 days the same process will be repeated again with new people. Only if 90 percent correct results are obtained both times will he be given the reward of 80 lakhs. 44 Years of Reputation versus 'Babagiri' Committee convener Shyam Manav, adopting a very aggressive stance, said, "We have been saying for the past 44 years that there is no divine power in this world. If Dhirendra Shastri proves himself, then I will bow at his feet, shut down my organization and become his devotee." The committee gave an interesting example comparing Baba's claims with modern technology. They said that in today's era, facial recognition technology at airports does similar work. Without looking at any papers, one can get information about a person's name, passport and booking details. 'Maharaj is running away from the challenge' The committee also states that Dhirendra Shastri will never accept this challenge. The committee alleges that the Baba plants his own people in his court and extracts their information in 5 minutes through photos or other means. The committee questioned that when big people like the Chief Minister of Maharashtra bow down before him, what was the Baba afraid of? It has been alleged that both Maharaj and the committee know that he does not possess any divine powers. They are merely exploiting superstition to deceive people. According to the committee, "He knew that if he participated in this impartial challenge, his 'Babagiri' business would shut down. That is why he has once again fled from this challenge." Shyam Manav had given a challenge three years ago as well In January 2023, Dhirendra Shastri had gone to Nagpur for Katha Vachana (religious discourse). At that time too, Shyam Manav had challenged him. The challenge was that Dhirendra Shastri should publicly provide accurate information about 10 people - such as name, phone number and personal details. These 10 people should be chosen by Shyam Manav, not by Baba's team. He had said that if Shastri could prove this, he would give him 30 lakh rupees. Dhirendra Shastri accepted the challenge He accepted the challenge and said that whoever has an 'itch', come to the court. Whatever knowledge and power we have, we will present it. We are not magicians. Whatever inspiration God gives us, we will guide people accordingly.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath proposes 2-day weekly WFH after PM Modi’s appeal:Are demerits like social isolation being overlooked?
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has proposed a two-day weekly work-from-home (WFH) model for employees in large industrial units, IT companies and startups as part of a wider push to save fuel and reduce costs. The state government's move comes after Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to adopt energy-saving practices, including work from home (WFH). While the policy may offer benefits such as lower commuting expenses, are we overlooking possible demerits like loneliness, social isolation and mental strain? Let us take a closer look at what working from home actually means in practice. How many companies are offering WFH jobs in India? Remote work in India is no longer limited to a few firms. Globally, the trend is stronger. In India, major companies such as Infosys, Wipro, and HCLTech have adopted hybrid or flexible work models in recent years. In what ways does working from home benefit the nation? Working from home can support the wider economy in several practical ways. First, it helps businesses reduce operational costs. Second, WFH expands access to jobs beyond major cities. Third, digital workflows encourage investment in broadband, cloud systems and cybersecurity. Finally, flexible work models can improve employee retention. What are the salary differences between a WFH job and an on-site job? In most cases, salary depends on skill level, experience and industry, not simply on whether the job is remote or office-based. However, some differences may appear in allowances. For an individual, does WFH have more advantages or disadvantages? For knowledge-based roles, such as IT, design, writing or analysis, WFH often increases autonomy. However, the disadvantages are real. Conclusion: For most skilled, digitally based roles, advantages slightly outweigh disadvantages. Without discipline and support, disadvantages can become stronger. In which sectors can WFH never be an option? Some sectors require physical presence because the work depends on machinery, direct service or on-site supervision. In these cases, remote work is either impossible or extremely limited. How can people protect themselves from WFH scams? Graphics: Anas Shakir

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh CM launches BJP training camp in Gorakhpur:Yogi Adityanath says party became world’s largest political organisation in less than 50 years
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the BJP District Training Camp in Gorakhpur on Sunday. The programme was organised at a resort in the Sahjanwa Assembly constituency as part of the two-day training session being held on May 17 and 18. Addressing party workers, the Chief Minister said the Bharatiya Janata Party had become the world’s largest political party within less than 50 years of its formation. He said the BJP had independently formed governments at the Centre and in 22 states across the country. ‘Nation first, party second, individual last’ Yogi Adityanath said the BJP was the only political party in the country and the world that had consistently upheld the principle of “Nation first, party second and individual interest last”. He said the party had always worked with nationalism as its core ideology. See 5 pictures CM recalls sacrifice of Syama Prasad Mookerjee The Chief Minister said Syama Prasad Mookerjee had entered Kashmir to protest against the permit system along with his associates. According to Yogi Adityanath, Mookerjee was arrested and later died in a Jammu and Kashmir jail. He said the sacrifice of leaders who fought for the country helped strengthen the foundation of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. Tribute to Deendayal Upadhyaya The Chief Minister also remembered Deendayal Upadhyaya, saying he advocated ensuring that government welfare schemes reached even the last person in society. He said Upadhyaya later became president of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and also faced betrayal and an untimely death. According to Yogi Adityanath, Upadhyaya understood that political stability was essential for development and worked continuously towards strengthening the organisation. BJP’s political journey explained The Chief Minister said the credit for the formation of the first non-Congress government in 1967 also went to Deendayal Upadhyaya. He said the Bharatiya Jana Sangh later entered a new phase under Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Lal Krishna Advani. During that period, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh merged with the Janata Party to strengthen the democracy movement. He said the BJP was later formed on April 6, 1980, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He further said- The BJP had won only two MPs initially. Today, it has become the world’s largest political party. ‘BJP workers must remain different from other parties’ Yogi Adityanath urged BJP workers to uphold the party’s values and ideals in their personal conduct. He said if BJP workers began behaving like leaders and workers of parties such as the Congress, SP, BSP, RJD, TMC and DMK, society would never respect them. According to him, BJP workers must function differently while respecting India and Indian values. He also stressed the need to strengthen the BJP organisation through better coordination and strong booth-level structures. He also said- Our booth should remain our central focus. ‘BJP gave women the Right to Live with dignity’ The Chief Minister said the BJP had supported the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya in 1986 as part of its commitment to cultural nationalism. He said a grand Ram Temple had now been constructed under the double-engine government. According to him, India had emerged as a beacon of hope globally. He also said the BJP had given women the right to live with dignity by banning the practice of triple talaq. Yogi Adityanath added that reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies through the Women’s Reservation Act had been introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 2-day training camp and Janata Darshan The BJP District Training Camp will continue for two days on May 17 and 18. As mobile phones were prohibited during the programme, BJP workers deposited their phones at Assembly-wise counters set up at the venue. Before attending the event, Yogi Adityanath also heard grievances of around 150 people during the Janata Darshan programme organised at Gorakhnath Temple.

stories.title: Woman manager suicide case — Action after CM Yogi’s intervention:Accused businessman’s apartment demolished with bulldozer; hotel and 3 cars seized
stories.summary: A bulldozer was used on Saturday to demolish illegal construction at the apartment of the main accused businessman in the suicide case of salon manager Ratna Singh (31) in Gomtinagar Extension, Lucknow. Earlier, the accused’s hotel, salon and three vehicles had also been seized by the police. Ratna, who worked as a manager at businessman Sharad Singh’s salon, died by suicide on May 12 by hanging herself. Before taking the step, she recorded a video accusing businessman Sharad Singh, his wife Pallavi Singh and several others of harassment. Ratna’s father, Sudhir Singh, later lodged a named FIR against five people. Father met CM Yogi over delay in action Alleging inaction by the police, Sudhir Singh met Yogi Adityanath on May 15. On May 16, he released a video claiming that Sharad Singh was evading arrest by using his influence. He alleged that despite registration of the case, the police had failed to take concrete action. Sudhir said he had appealed to the Chief Minister for justice and was assured that strict action would be taken. Following the meeting with the Chief Minister, action in the case intensified. Police announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each on the accused and formed six teams to trace them. Raids are currently underway in Lucknow and several other districts. 5 pictures of police action Ratna recorded video before suicide Ratna Singh, a resident of Gorakhpur, died by suicide on May 12 in Shalimar Vista Apartment in Gomtinagar Extension after recording a video message. In the video, she made serious allegations against businessman Sharad Singh, his wife, along with Mangal Yadav, Vaishali and Prashant Sharma. Based on a complaint filed by her father Sudhir Singh, Gomtinagar Extension police registered a case against the accused. Within 24 hours, police arrested only one accused, Mangalnath Yadav, who reportedly worked at Sharad Singh’s hotel. Father Accuses Police of Negligence In the video released on May 16, Sudhir Singh said his daughter worked at Virasat Company in Lucknow and had named Sharad Singh and his associates before ending her life. According to him, Ratna had alleged physical and mental harassment by the accused, which drove her to suicide. Sudhir said- A case was registered on May 12 against the named accused, but so far only one arrest has been made. On the evening of May 15, I met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who assured me that justice would be delivered and strict action would be taken. I have faith in the justice system. May 16 has passed, now let us see what happens next See the pictures of the accused- ‘She was harassed for opposing wrongdoing’ Sudhir Singh alleged that his daughter had come to know about the “dark activities” of accused Sharad Singh and began facing harassment after opposing them. He claimed Ratna did not support the alleged illegal activities being carried out under the guise of the hotel business. “She was very brave, but eventually broke down. To stop the matter from reaching the family, she chose death,” he alleged. He further claimed that negligence by the police allowed Sharad Singh and the other accused to escape. Two major actions taken after complaint to CM DCP East Dr Diksha Sharma said - A reward of Rs 25,000 each had been announced for the absconding accused. Six police teams, including surveillance units, have been formed to arrest them, and raids are being conducted in Lucknow and other districts. All the accused will be in police custody soon.

stories.title: Bulldozer action sparks protest outside Lucknow court:Scuffle breaks out between police and lawyers; 6 bulldozers, 300 policemen deployed
stories.summary: A demolition drive against illegal encroachments began outside the Lucknow District Court at 9 am on Saturday. Around 240 illegal structures, including lawyers’ chambers and roadside shops, are being demolished using six bulldozers. As the administration’s team arrived with bulldozers in the morning, more than 100 lawyers gathered at the site. They raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest by sitting on the ground. Scuffle breaks out during protest When police attempted to remove the protesters, an argument broke out between the police, lawyers and shopkeepers. The situation soon escalated into pushing and shoving. Police later used batons to disperse the protesting lawyers and shopkeepers from the area. At present, four ACPs, personnel from the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), and more than 300 police personnel have been deployed at the spot. Encroachments had occupied roads, footpaths and drains According to the administration, lawyers’ chambers and photocopy shops had been constructed illegally by occupying roads, footpaths and drainage areas, causing inconvenience to commuters. The matter had reached the Allahabad High Court, following which the court ordered the removal of illegal encroachments. The municipal corporation later issued notices directing occupants to remove the encroachments. While some people voluntarily cleared the structures, a large number failed to comply, leading to the demolition action. See photos-

stories.title: Will BSP lose its national party status?:Fails to secure 1% votes in Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; may lose Rajya Sabha presence too
stories.summary: There are currently six national parties in the country, BJP, Indian National Congress (Congress), Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI-M), Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and National People's Party (NPP). However, BSP’s status as a national party is now under serious threat. The party failed to secure even 1% of the vote share in the Assembly elections in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. BSP also has no representation in the Lok Sabha and only one MP in the Rajya Sabha. The key question now is how serious the threat to BSP’s national party status has become, why the party has managed to retain recognition so far, and why the upcoming Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand are crucial for its survival. Poor performance in Bengal, Kerala and Tamil Nadu BSP fielded candidates on 152 out of 294 seats in the West Bengal Assembly elections, but all candidates forfeited their deposits. The party secured only 1.17 lakh votes, accounting for 0.18% of the total vote share. In Kerala, where Assembly elections were held on 140 seats, BSP contested 55 constituencies. The party received only 33,125 votes, or 0.15% of the vote share. Similarly, in Tamil Nadu, BSP fielded candidates on 118 out of 234 Assembly seats and managed just 53,369 votes, equivalent to 0.11% of the vote share. Across all three states combined, BSP received only 2.04 lakh votes, failing to meet the criteria required for recognition as a state party in any of them. BSP opened account in Bihar, but vote share stayed below 2% In the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, BSP contested 192 out of 243 seats. The party managed to win only one seat and secured a total of 8.13 lakh votes, translating to 1.62% vote share. Despite opening its account in the state, BSP still failed to fulfil the criteria required for recognition as a state party in Bihar. Weak performance in Delhi, Haryana, Maharashtra and Jharkhand Delhi In the February 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, BSP contested 68 out of 70 seats. None of its candidates managed to save their deposits. The party received around 55,000 votes, or 0.58% vote share. Haryana During the October 2024 Haryana Assembly elections, BSP contested in alliance with Indian National Lok Dal (INLD). The party fielded candidates on 35 out of 90 seats, but all lost their deposits. BSP secured 2.52 lakh votes, amounting to 1.82% vote share. Maharashtra In the November 2024 Maharashtra Assembly elections, BSP contested 237 out of 288 seats. All candidates forfeited their deposits, while the party’s vote share stood at just 0.48%. Jharkhand BSP fielded candidates on all 81 Assembly seats in the 2024 Jharkhand elections held between November and December. The party failed to win a single seat, and its vote share remained below 1%. BSP had earlier saved its national party status in 2014 BSP was granted national party status in 1997. However, in 2014, the party came close to losing this recognition after failing to win a single Lok Sabha seat. Its national vote share had also dropped to 4.19%. In August 2014, the Election Commission issued show-cause notices to BSP, Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and Communist Party of India (CPI), asking why their national party status should not be revoked. BSP then sought additional time from the Election Commission and requested that the review be deferred until after the Delhi Assembly election results. In 2016, the Election Commission amended the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. Under the revised rules, the review process for national parties, which earlier took place every five years, was extended to once every 10 years. The amendment provided temporary relief to BSP, NCP and CPI until 2019. Later, BSP managed to secure more than 6% vote share in Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Bihar and Punjab. This helped the party retain its recognition as a state party in multiple states and, in turn, preserve its national party status.

stories.title: UP braces for severe heatwave:Temperature nears 45°C in Banda, alert in 23 districts
stories.summary: As storms and rain subsided across Uttar Pradesh, intense heat returned to the state, with temperatures nearing 45°C. The sky remained clear in most cities from Sunday morning, while bright sunshine and low wind speed increased humidity levels. The Meteorological Department has issued a heatwave alert for 23 cities today. Rising daytime temperatures are expected to intensify the heat, with temperatures likely to continue increasing over the next five days. From May 20 onwards, the heatwave is expected to become more severe, affecting more than half of the state’s cities. No rainfall was recorded anywhere in the state during the past 24 hours. Banda remained the hottest city for the fifth consecutive day, recording a maximum temperature of 44.8°C. Bijnor was the coolest city, where the minimum temperature settled at 20.2°C. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- The monsoon is expected to reach Kerala around May 26. Based on current estimates, it may enter Uttar Pradesh through Gorakhpur around June 18. However, this is only a probable date. The exact timeline will be assessed after the monsoon advances from Kerala. At present, there is no immediate relief from the heat. The entire state will remain under severe heat conditions for at least the next week. See photos- Weather forecast for the next 5 days May 18- Strong sunshine is expected across East and West UP. Heatwave conditions may prevail during the afternoon, while winds could blow at speeds of 20–30 kmph. May 19- Light cloud cover may appear in some areas, but no rainfall is expected. Heatwave conditions are likely during the afternoon. May 20- The weather will remain dry in West UP, with no storm or rain alert. Some areas of East UP may receive light rainfall. May 21- Light showers may occur in parts of north-eastern Purvanchal, while severe heat will continue across West UP. May 22- The weather is expected to remain clear in West UP, where heatwave conditions will persist. Some eastern districts may receive light rain. Weather conditions in major cities Lucknow Bright sunshine and clear skies have prevailed since morning, accompanied by hot winds. The maximum temperature is expected to reach 41°C, while the minimum may remain around 27°C. Intense heat is also likely during the night. Kanpur Strong sunshine has continued since morning, and a heatwave alert has been issued for the afternoon. People stepping outdoors were seen covering their faces with cloth, gamchas and angocchas. No relief from the heat is expected for at least a week. Gorakhpur Temperatures are rising due to strong sunshine and westerly winds. Roads witnessed thinner crowds during the day. Intense sunshine is expected to trouble residents, while humid conditions may continue at night. Meerut The weather has remained clear since morning with bright sunshine. For the first time this May, the temperature may cross 40°C. Morning temperatures were already recorded above 30°C, while wind speeds could remain around 10–12 kmph. Ghaziabad Bright sunshine has prevailed since morning, with severe heat expected during the day. The temperature was recorded at 29°C in the early morning, while the maximum may touch 40.8°C later in the day. Wind speed is expected to remain around 10 kmph. UP likely to receive below-normal monsoon rainfall The Meteorological Department has predicted below-normal rainfall in Uttar Pradesh between June and September. India Meteorological Department Director General Dr M. Mohapatra said weather conditions resembling La Niña in the Pacific Ocean are now showing signs of shifting towards El Niño conditions, which could reduce rainfall. This indicates that the southwest monsoon may remain weaker than normal this year. He added that low snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March could also affect the monsoon. Last year’s monsoon was 10–15% above normal According to the Meteorological Department, Uttar Pradesh received an average rainfall of 870–900 mm during the 2025 monsoon season between June and September. This was around 10–15% higher than the normal monsoon average. Crops damaged by storms and rain; Yogi assures support Heavy rain and storms on Wednesday and Thursday caused widespread damage to crops across the state. Vegetable crops such as cucumber, gherkin and watermelon were among the worst affected. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Thursday that the government stands with farmers and the public during this difficult period. He said authorities are continuously monitoring the situation to ensure timely assistance reaches those in need, and warned that negligence by officials during relief operations would not be tolerated. Why is the weather fluctuating? According to the Meteorological Department, weather conditions in the hills of Uttarakhand have been changing continuously, with snowfall in some areas and rainfall in others. On certain days, the weather clears with strong sunshine. Similar fluctuations are expected to continue over the next few days, affecting Uttar Pradesh as well. Winds blowing from the hills have helped keep temperatures comparatively lower at times and are also creating conditions favourable for rainfall.

stories.title: 111 dead as violent storms batter Uttar Pradesh:From AC blasts to sudden daytime darkness, extreme weather shocks residents across several districts
stories.summary: From people being thrown by violent winds to air-conditioners exploding in scorching heat and cities turning dark in the middle of the morning, Uttar Pradesh has witnessed a series of extreme weather events over the past few weeks. After unseasonal rain and storms, temperatures are now expected to climb again to 45°C–47°C by the end of May. At the same time, meteorologists say the monsoon could arrive nearly a week earlier than usual. However, despite the intense heat, monsoon rains are coming 7 days earlier to provide relief to people this time. The monsoon will enter UP by June 18. Why is the weather changing so rapidly in UP, find out in Sunday Big Story Three incidents that shocked Uttar Pradesh Man blown nearly 100 metres during storm On May 13, winds blowing at nearly 90 kmph struck Bareilly. During the storm, a man was reportedly lifted almost 50 feet into the air and thrown nearly 100 metres into a maize field. He suffered fractures in one arm and one leg. Multiple AC explosions amid extreme heat Between April and May, at least six buildings in Noida and Ghaziabad reported air-conditioner explosions. Officials and technicians believe the compressors failed because they could not withstand temperatures touching 45°C. Daytime turned into ‘night’ in Lucknow On the morning of May 4, Lucknow witnessed sudden darkness around 9 am despite clear weather earlier in the day. Drivers were forced to switch on headlights as thick clouds covered the city. Heavy rain and strong winds followed shortly afterward. Uttar Pradesh witnessing extreme temperature swings Meteorologists say Uttar Pradesh has experienced both record-breaking heat and sudden weather reversals this season. 37 UP cities among world’s hottest On April 23, 92 Indian cities featured among the world’s 100 hottest locations, including 37 from Uttar Pradesh. After Maharashtra’s Khed district, the hottest places included Mughalsarai, Amethi, Varanasi and Ghazipur in Uttar Pradesh. On April 27, Banda recorded 47.6°C, making it the hottest place in the world that day. Districts including Prayagraj, Chitrakoot and Hamirpur also recorded temperatures above 45°C for several consecutive days. Residents feared May and June would become unbearable. Sudden shift from heatwave to rainstorms However, the expected escalation in heat did not happen immediately. In the first week of May, temperatures suddenly dropped as rainfall began in western Uttar Pradesh before spreading across the state. On May 4 and 5, almost every district in Uttar Pradesh received rain. The state recorded 27.4 mm rainfall during the first week of May — nearly seven times higher than the average May rainfall of 3.3 mm. Then, on May 13, violent storms and strong winds killed 111 people across the state. Officials said it was the highest single-day death toll caused by weather-related incidents in the past decade. Prayagraj reported 21 deaths, while Bhadohi recorded 17 fatalities. The deaths even drew condolences from Russian President Vladimir Putin. Why is the weather changing so rapidly? Scientists say the dramatic weather swings are being driven by atmospheric instability caused by the collision of cold and warm air systems. Cold air above, hot air below Dr. Atul Singh, senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow, explained that western disturbances were pushing dry and cold winds across the upper atmosphere. At the same time, warm and moisture-laden winds were moving from the east at lower atmospheric levels. Clash of air masses triggered instability When cold, dry air collided with warm, humid air, the atmosphere became unstable. Meteorologists say this instability intensified because a cyclonic circulation had already formed over western Uttar Pradesh. As hot air rose rapidly and collided with colder air above, it triggered violent thunderstorms, lightning and powerful windstorms. Scientists say this explains why storms became so intense in places like Bareilly and why cities like Lucknow experienced sudden daytime darkness. Have such storms happened before? According to scientists, Uttar Pradesh has experienced major storms in previous years as well, particularly in 2016, 2018 and 2020. However, this year’s storms were unusually intense because wind speeds were significantly higher. Earlier storms typically recorded wind speeds between 60 and 80 kmph. This year, several regions witnessed speeds crossing 100 kmph. Meteorologists say wind intensity also depends on local geographical conditions, which is why one part of a district may record 110 kmph winds while another area experiences much lower speeds. They describe the current phase as a “pre-monsoon season,” though weather patterns this year are shifting much faster than usual. What is El Niño and why does it matter? Scientists believe another major reason behind the unusual weather is the warming of the Pacific Ocean, known as El Niño. El Niño refers to changes in sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean. This year, the eastern and central Pacific are significantly warmer than normal, with water temperatures reportedly touching 24°C. Meteorologists say when ocean temperatures rise sharply, weather patterns across India become unstable. This can result in both severe heatwaves and sudden storms or rainfall. However, scientists stress that El Niño alone does not control the monsoon. Several other atmospheric and oceanic factors also influence India’s weather system. Monsoon likely to arrive early Despite fears of extreme heat, meteorologists believe the monsoon may arrive earlier than expected. Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal playing key role Scientists say the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal are currently warmer than normal, creating large amounts of moisture. This has made monsoon winds “super active,” allowing the monsoon system to advance rapidly. Normally, the monsoon reaches Kerala around June 1. This year, it is expected to arrive by May 26 — nearly four days early. Uttar Pradesh could get monsoon by June 18 Weather experts now estimate that the monsoon could reach Uttar Pradesh by June 18. Earlier forecasts had suggested people in the state might have to wait until early July. Concern over weak monsoon and heatwaves The US weather agency National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has warned that a “super El Niño” is likely this year. Meteorologists fear this could weaken overall monsoon rainfall while increasing the risks of drought and prolonged heatwaves. What lies ahead? The India Meteorological Department has warned that intense heat is likely to return over the next 10 days. Districts such as Prayagraj, Banda and Chitrakoot are expected to see temperatures once again cross 45°C. Western Uttar Pradesh is also likely to experience severe heat conditions.

stories.title: Vinesh says ‘Jhukane ki taqat nahi kisi talwar mein’:Brij Bhushan calls it a ‘drama’, wrestler denied entry to Gonda wrestling event
stories.summary: The ongoing verbal clash between wrestler Vinesh Phogat and former Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has intensified, with both sides targeting each other indirectly on social media without taking names. The controversy resurfaced after the Senior National Ranking Wrestling Competition began on Sunday at Nandini Nagar Mahavidyalaya in Gonda, Uttar Pradesh, an institution linked to Brij Bhushan Singh. Vinesh was not allowed to participate in the event. Vinesh shares emotional post on X After being excluded from the tournament, Vinesh Phogat posted an emotional message on X. Soon afterwards, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh responded with a cryptic post of his own. Vinesh Phogat was planning to make her return to competitive wrestling through the National Open Ranking event. However, the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) issued her a show-cause notice and barred her from domestic competitions until June 26. The federation accused her of indiscipline and violating anti-doping regulations. According to WFI, she failed to complete the mandatory six-month notice period required under United World Wrestling rules for athletes returning from retirement. Vinesh had announced her retirement after being disqualified from the final of the 2024 Paris Olympics for being overweight. Sexual harassment allegations against Brij Bhushan Around three years ago, Vinesh Phogat accused Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexually harassing female wrestlers. Several women wrestlers, including Sakshi Malik and Bajrang Punia, joined protests against him at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in 2023. Vinesh is currently a Congress MLA from Julana in Haryana, while Brij Bhushan is a former BJP MP. One of his sons is currently an MP in Uttar Pradesh and another is an MLA. See pictures- Wrestling competition inaugurated by Brij Bhushan The 2026 Open Senior National Ranking Wrestling Competition is being held at the sports stadium of Nandini Nagar Mahavidyalaya in Gonda. On Sunday at 10 am, Wrestling Federation president Sanjay Singh and former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh inaugurated the tournament. They also met wrestlers and interacted with participants. However, shortly after the inauguration, Brij Bhushan left for another programme. In earlier years, he was often seen staying at such events to encourage wrestlers. Vinesh returned from Lucknow without participating Vinesh Phogat had travelled to Lucknow on Saturday night with plans to participate in the tournament in Gonda. However, she later returned without attending the event. WFI president Sanjay Singh said Vinesh Phogat had been served a notice over allegations of indiscipline. He warned that if her response was found unsatisfactory, stricter action, including a ban, could be imposed. He said, 'Vinesh has now become used to making allegations about everything. When she expressed her wish to participate, we took complete responsibility for her safety. It was our duty to bring her safely, arrange her matches and ensure her return.' He added that female wrestlers from across the country, including many from Haryana, were participating in the event and said questioning the federation’s system was unfair. Federation issued 15-page notice The Wrestling Federation alleged in a 15-page notice that Vinesh’s conduct during the Paris Olympics controversy had damaged the reputation of Indian wrestling permanently. The notice also claimed she violated the federation’s constitution, international wrestling rules and anti-doping guidelines. Vinesh had earlier questioned the security arrangements for her participation in Gonda. Following this, the WFI suspended her from domestic competitions until June 26. Wrestlers from 29 states are taking part More than 1,400 wrestlers from 29 states are participating in the three-day competition in Gonda. Freestyle wrestling bouts were held on the opening day on Sunday. The first match on Mat B in the 97 kg category was between Haryana’s Ashish and Sheetal Guliya. The second match in the same category featured UP’s Rajat against Haryana’s Alok Malik. The third bout was contested between Haryana’s Maan Kumar and UP’s Deepesh Kumar. Wrestling returns to Gonda after 3 years This is the first major wrestling competition being held in Gonda in three years. The last National Wrestling Competition organised here in 2023 was later cancelled by the Sports Ministry following allegations raised by protesting wrestlers against the Wrestling Federation of India. After the controversy in 2023, national-level wrestling events have now resumed in Gonda in 2026. How the sexual harassment controversy began ? On January 18, 2023, wrestlers Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik and Bajrang Punia launched a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and accused Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexually harassing female wrestlers. During the protest, Vinesh broke down in tears and alleged that Brij Bhushan and some coaches sexually harassed women wrestlers at national camps. She claimed Brij Bhushan stayed in the players’ hotel despite rules prohibiting it. She also alleged that after her defeat at the Tokyo Olympics, he had called her a “bad coin”. Brij Bhushan denied allegations Responding to the allegations at the time, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh denied all accusations and said no harassment had taken place. He stated that if the allegations were proven true, he would “hang himself”. He also described the wrestlers’ protest as politically sponsored and accused Congress Rajya Sabha MP Deepender Hooda of being behind it. Brij Bhushan further claimed that the protesting wrestlers were no longer fit to compete even at national-level tournaments.

stories.title: Tigress sits with 2 cubs before tourists:Bear and tiger came face to face in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve
stories.summary: A tigress was spotted resting with her two cubs in the middle of a road inside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Lakhimpur. The rare sight left tourists stunned when their safari jeep reached the spot on Saturday morning. The tourists immediately stopped their vehicle and quietly captured the thrilling moment on camera. After resting for some time, the tigress got up with her cubs and slowly moved back into the forest. Tourists witness tiger and bear face-off As the safari jeep moved further ahead, tourists witnessed another dramatic scene, a tiger and a bear standing face to face in the forest. Seeing the tense situation, the safari guide immediately instructed everyone to remain inside the vehicle. For nearly 10 minutes, both animals stared at each other without moving. Eventually, the tiger changed its path and disappeared into the jungle, avoiding a confrontation. The incident took place in the Sonaripur range of the reserve and was recorded on camera by guide Raju. The video has since gone viral on social media. See the pictures- Wildlife photographers from Gujarat were on Safari According to officials, a team of wildlife photographers from Gujarat was on a safari in the Sonaripur range on Saturday. Tiger Reserve guide Raju accompanied the group during the visit. During the safari, they first encountered the tigress sitting on the road with her cubs. Later, while returning from the forest, they came across the tiger and bear face-off. Bears avoid areas with High Tiger Movement Wildlife experts say that in core forest areas where tiger density and patrolling are very high, bears generally avoid those routes and move towards safer and denser parts of the forest to reduce the risk of conflict with large carnivores. This made the rare encounter between the tiger and the bear even more unusual for the tourists present at the spot. Tiger population estimated between 135 and 153 According to tiger census data from 2022 to 2024, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve is estimated to have a tiger population of between 135 and 153. The reserve is home to several famous tigers, including the “Beldanda” tigress, known for giving birth to 13 cubs, and “Gabbar”, often referred to as the “Don of Dudhwa”. Kishanpur Range has highest Tiger density The Kishanpur range of the reserve has the highest tiger density because of the abundance of prey animals. Officials estimate that nearly five tigers are found per 100 square kilometres in this area. In the main Dudhwa forest area, the dense Sal forests support an average of two tigers per 100 square kilometres. Distinct identity of the Terai Forest Dudhwa forest spreads across nearly 490 square kilometres and is known for its rich Terai ecosystem. The forest contains dense Sal and Teak trees along with vast grasslands locally known as “Phanta”. These grasslands serve as an ideal habitat for animals such as deer and swamp deer, also known as barasingha. Rivers, including the Suheli and Mohana flow through the reserve, helping maintain marshlands, ponds, and lakes that remain filled with water throughout the year. Tigers, Rhinos and Barasingha are major attractions Dudhwa Tiger Reserve is considered one of the richest biodiversity zones in the region. More than 135 Bengal tigers roam freely across the forest. The reserve is also home to one-horned rhinoceroses brought from Assam’s Kaziranga National Park, which have now successfully established a population of more than 50 animals. Dudhwa also holds special importance for the conservation of barasingha. A significant portion of the world’s swamp deer population survives in the reserve’s marshy grasslands.

stories.title: 6 new ministers inducted into Yogi cabinet, 2 promoted:Bhupendra Chaudhary and Manoj Pandey take oath as cabinet ministers
stories.summary: The Yogi cabinet underwent its second expansion on Sunday. Two cabinet ministers and four Ministers of State were inducted, while two existing Ministers of State were promoted to Ministers of State (Independent Charge). The oath-taking ceremony was held at Raj Bhavan. Former BJP state president Bhupendra Chaudhary was the first to take oath. He was followed by MLA Manoj Pandey, who had rebelled against the Samajwadi Party. Both have been inducted as cabinet ministers. Ajit Pal took oath third, followed by Somendra Tomar. Both were previously Ministers of State and have now been elevated to Ministers of State (Independent Charge). 4 leaders inducted as Ministers of State Krishna Paswan, Kailash Rajput, Surendra Diler and Hansraj Vishwakarma then took oath as Ministers of State. Krishna Paswan arrived wearing a ‘Radhe-Radhe’ stole, while Surendra Diler was dressed in saffron attire. After taking oath, Krishna Paswan raised slogans of “Jai Shri Ram”. Social representation in cabinet expansion Among the newly inducted ministers, one belongs to the Brahmin community, three are from OBC groups and two are from Dalit communities. There is speculation that Bhupendra Chaudhary may be assigned the Public Works Department (PWD). The ministry has remained with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath since Jitin Prasada moved to the Centre as a minister. Yogi government now at full ministerial strength With the latest expansion, the Yogi government has reached its full strength of 60 ministers. The cabinet now includes 23 cabinet ministers, 16 Ministers of State (Independent Charge) and 21 Ministers of State. The first expansion of the Yogi cabinet took place on 5 March 2024, just ahead of the Lok Sabha elections. stories.title: 7.28 lakh meters to be converted to postpaid:Process started in 7 districts of Gorakhpur-Basti division
stories.summary: After public opposition, the government has decided to convert prepaid smart meters to postpaid. The number of such meters in the 7 districts of Gorakhpur and Basti divisions is 7 lakh 28 thousand 763. The process of converting them to postpaid has started. For now, the hassle of recharging has been eliminated, and no one's electricity will be cut off. After the meters become postpaid, connections of those who do not pay their electricity bills on time will be disconnected. After depositing the money, it will be reconnected in auto mode. The work of installing new meters in place of old meters in premises will continue, but these will not be converted to prepaid mode. The work of operating in prepaid mode had started in September 2025 The operation of postpaid smart meters in prepaid mode was initiated in September 2025. Messages were sent to consumers for this purpose. They were informed that the outstanding dues from before the operation in prepaid mode would be deposited in installments along with the prepaid meter recharge. This means that when a consumer recharged through the prepaid meter for electricity consumption, the outstanding dues of the old meter would also be deposited from that amount. Know how the problem increased While an awareness campaign was being run regarding electricity consumption through prepaid meters, even after depositing money, no accurate information was being recorded in the UPPCL Smart app regarding outstanding dues and old arrears in the meter, which was increasing the problem. Consumers alleged that even after recharging the meter, arrears were continuously showing in the app. Also, electricity was getting cut off at any time. Those who don't have Android phones were not able to find out anything at all. In recent days, women in the Gangtahi sub-center area of Sahjanwa block had uprooted prepaid meters from premises and staged a protest. Protests were taking place at several locations in the state. Consumer Adarsh from the Taramandal area said that despite continuous bill payments and running only one AC, the app sometimes shows a maximum demand of six kilowatts and sometimes shows something else. Even after recharging the meter several times in a single day, the outstanding amount does not get cleared. Ban on installing prepaid meters was imposed on April 18, but they are being installed on new connections A ban was imposed on installing smart prepaid meters on April 18 until technical flaws were investigated. Before this ban, they had already been installed at 7 lakh 22 thousand premises in the Gorakhpur-Basti division. Smart prepaid meters are to be installed at 26 lakh 95 thousand 826 premises in both divisions. Now, old meters are not being removed and replaced with smart prepaid meters, but the process of installing them on new connections will continue. It is being assumed that after converting all prepaid meters to postpaid, only postpaid meters will be installed for new connections as well. After converting prepaid meters to postpaid, messages for negative bills will not come. A ban has also been imposed on disconnecting connections. Now, consumers will get a lot of relief. This is the situation in the districts of Gorakhpur and Basti divisions

stories.title: Labour organisations stage protest demonstration in Lucknow:Supported workers' movement in Noida; demonstrators allege leaders behind agitation were made to disappear
stories.summary: Protest demonstration at Charbagh Railway Station in Lucknow. Under the banner of the All India Central Council of Trade Union, various labor organizations called for a march from Charbagh to the CM's residence. People from various social and labor organizations have taken to the streets against the workers' protest that took place in Noida in recent days, and the police action against it. The protesters were moving towards the Chief Minister's residence from Charbagh, carrying red flags and posters in their hands. The protesters were stopped by installing triple-layer barricading at Charbagh. The protesters said that the lathi charge was brutally carried out on workers in Noida. Workers in Noida had taken to the streets for their rights - getting respectable wages and facilities is the right of every worker. But instead of giving these workers their rights, police action was taken against them.

stories.title: Weather to worsen again in UP after 2 days:Storm and rain alert from May 12; Jhansi hottest, temperature rises 5°C within 2 days
stories.summary: The spell of storms and rain in UP has paused for two days. Since Sunday morning, the weather across the entire state has been clear. Bright sunshine has emerged. However, light cool winds are reducing the effect of the sun. There is no alert for storms or rain anywhere on Sunday. After about 7 days, the day temperature reached 40 °C on Saturday. On Sunday too, the mercury is expected to remain between 40 °C and 43 °C. The Meteorological Department says that the effect of the current western disturbance has completely ended. However, from May 12, the weather will deteriorate again. A new western disturbance is becoming active. This will start another spell of rain. Conditions like storms and hail will develop. Speaking of the last 24 hours, there was no rain anywhere in the state. Jhansi remained the hottest. The maximum temperature here was recorded at 40 °C. Two days ago, that is on May 8, the mercury was recorded at 34.8 °C. This means there has been a jump of 5°C. Sultanpur's night was the coldest. The minimum temperature here was recorded at 19 °C. Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh of the Regional Meteorological Center informed- The spell of rain that has been continuing in UP since April 30 has taken a break. There will be intense heat for 2 days. Nights may also remain hot in some areas. However, there will be relief from heatwaves for now. A new western disturbance will become active from May 12. Conditions like rain, thunderstorms, and hail will develop. Condition of Major Cities Why the fluctuations in weather? The Meteorological Department says that the weather in the mountains of Uttarakhand is constantly changing. There is snowfall in some places and rain in others. Meanwhile, on some days, the weather clears up with sunshine. Such fluctuations are expected for the next few days. Its direct impact is visible in UP. The winds coming from the mountains are keeping the weather cold. They are creating systems favorable for rain. What will the weather be like for the next 5 days? Forecast of less rainfall in monsoon this year Private weather agency Skymet Weather has released the forecast for this year's monsoon. According to it, monsoon rainfall may be 6% less than normal. The normal average rainfall in the country during the 4 months of monsoon from June to September is 868.6 mm. Less than normal monsoon means rainfall will be between 90% to 95%. The agency has forecast 94% rainfall. There will be normal rainfall in June, but the decline will start from July, and the monsoon will weaken in August and September. Especially in August-September, there are indications of a more rainfall deficit. UP will also receive less rainfall during monsoon, know the reason Between June and September, Uttar Pradesh is also likely to receive below-normal rainfall. Director General of the Meteorological Department, Dr. M Mahapatra, said that this year there are signs of La Niña-like conditions ending in the Pacific Ocean and moving towards El Niño, which will cause less rainfall. This means there are indications that the south-west monsoon will be weaker than normal this year. Additionally, the reduced snow formation in the Northern Hemisphere during January-March this year may also affect the monsoon. Know about El Niño and La Niña
